skill.description: Document AI use cases for EU AI Act governance, inspect code or interview users, then validate and submit confirmed manifests to KI-Register.
skill.summary: Create validated KI-Register AI use case documentation for governance review.
skill.author: Egonso

security_audit.summary: Most static command detections are Markdown paths or documentation references, but several instructions direct the agent to run local Node CLI commands. The skill also submits governance manifests to a KI-Register API endpoint after explicit human confirmation. No prompt injection or covert credential exfiltration was found.

remediation.suggestion: State that studio-agent commands execute local code, require user confirmation before running them, and prefer a trusted or pinned CLI source.
Keep the explicit confirmation step and show the destination endpoint, register, and manifest summary before every submission.

remediation.issue: Shell export example for API keys
remediation.suggestion: Prefer secret-store or CLI onboarding instructions over inline export examples that may remain in shell history.

content.value_statement: AI governance records are hard to create from code, interviews, and operational context. This skill guides capture, validation, review, and confirmed KI-Register submission.
actual_capabilities: Creates use case records for AI applications, processes, and workflows.
Inspects local code and documents for evidence-backed workflow details.
Guides stakeholder interviews to fill missing governance fields.
Produces a manifest and README for team review.
Validates manifests with the Agent Kit CLI before submission.
Submits confirmed records to KI-Register when credentials are available.
limitations: It depends on the local Agent Kit CLI or compatible schema for validation and submission.
It cannot provide legal advice or determine final EU AI Act classification.
It needs reliable source evidence or stakeholder answers for complete records.
It submits only after explicit confirmation and valid KI-Register credentials.

use_cases.title: Prepare Governance Records
use_cases.description: Document an AI workflow with purpose, owner, data categories, controls, risks, and review artifacts.

use_cases.title: Map AI Features From Code
use_cases.description: Inspect a repository and turn visible routes, prompts, scripts, and docs into a reviewable use case draft.

use_cases.title: Collect Supplier Evidence
use_cases.description: Interview stakeholders and capture the facts needed for procurement, vendor review, and internal AI governance.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Interview Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to interview me about an AI workflow and create a KI-Register use case draft. Ask one question at a time.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to inspect this project and document any AI application or workflow with evidence-backed facts and unknowns.

prompt_templates.title: Validate an Existing Manifest
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my existing KI-Register use case files, validate the manifest, and list missing governance fields.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Confirmed Submission
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to prepare a validated manifest for KI-Register submission. Show the summary, destination, and blockers before asking for confirmation.

output_examples.input: A compliance lead asks for a record of a customer support AI workflow.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a plain-language use case summary, required governance fields, missing evidence, and a validated manifest path.

output_examples.input: An engineering team points the skill at a repository with AI routes and prompt files.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies candidate systems, records evidence-backed data categories, lists unknowns, and prepares files for human review.

output_examples.input: A registered team wants to submit a confirmed manifest.
output_examples.output: The skill validates locally, asks for explicit approval, then submits only when credentials and register details are available.

best_practices: Review generated summaries with the owner before validation or submission.
Keep KI-Register API keys in environment variables or a secret store.
Mark uncertain AI Act details as unknown for specialist review.
anti_patterns: Do not submit inferred records without explicit human approval.
Do not store API keys in manifests, README files, logs, or screenshots.
Do not overstate risk class when source evidence is incomplete.

faq.question: Does this skill decide EU AI Act risk class?
faq.answer: No. It documents facts for governance review and leaves uncertain classification decisions for qualified reviewers.

faq.question: Can it work from a codebase only?
faq.answer: Yes. It can inspect local files and mark unsupported details as unknown for follow-up.

faq.question: Can it interview business users?
faq.answer: Yes. It can ask targeted questions about purpose, data, controls, human review, and artifacts.

faq.question: Will it submit data automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill requires a visible summary and explicit human confirmation before submission.

faq.question: What credentials are needed for submission?
faq.answer: Submission needs a KI-Register API key and register identifier available through approved local configuration.

faq.question: What files does it produce?
faq.answer: It produces a machine-readable manifest and a human-readable README for review workflows.
